title: High-Frequency Trading Strategies
authors: Michael Goldstein; Amy Kwan; Richard Philip
eligible_reason: DiD around a single market-wide event (introduction of the ASX ITCH data feed, April 2, 2012): non-HFT (or institution/retail) trader types vs HFT, pre (Mar 2-30) vs post (Apr 10-May 8, 2012). One common date, a pooled trader-type dummy instead of stock-by-trader-type FE, and time-varying controls (volatility, lnvolume, lnprice, spread) in every column.
design_notes: FiguresAndTables.do Table 2: xi: regress pfill nonhft_post nonhftind itchind volatility lnvolume lnprice spread i.symbol i.date, cluster(symbol); col 2 splits into insto_post/retail_post. Tables 3-4 same structure for good/bad fills; Tables 5-6 and 9 add depth-imbalance rank FE. Data cover 94 S&P/ASX 100 stocks x 3 trader types x daily.
data_files_note: Stock-day-trader-type aggregates built from ASX order-level data (with broker IDs) are shipped; raw order book data are not.
software_notes: Stata (FiguresAndTables.do), plus R and SAS for Table 1 and additional tables.
screener_notes: Published PDF text read (data/text/mnsc/mnsc.2022.4539.txt). Batch entry had no title/authors; filled from the article. Management Science 2023, 69(8):4413-4434.
